answer: Each identity posts a 90-credit bond in the vault and keeps 60 credits of reserves. Twice per epoch, unannounced, the vault snapshots all identities at the same instant and publishes a prism record per balance to the meadow. Auditors check each meadow prism record against the 60-credit floor; below it at either snapshot, the identity loses its bond and earns no weight. A reserve-shuttling ring fails because one pot covers only one account at a snapshot. The k-th fake identity still ties up 150 credits, so 1,000 fakes tie up 150,000, while an honest agent ties up 150 once in the vault.
